newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's top industry group blasts France.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's top industry group blasts France.

text.p: South Korea's top industry group on Wednesday attacked as discriminatory France's decision to scuttle the sale of Thomson Multimedia, a unit of Thomson SA, to Daewoo Electronics.

In a letter to the French ambassador to Seoul, the Federation of Korean Industries "expressed worries about the French government's discriminatory practices towards non-European companies", a federation statement said.
"We also expressed the shock and regret of the South Korean business community concerning the decision made on non-economic grounds and for reasons that cannot be understood," the statement added.
Earlier, the vice president of Daewoo Electronics, Nam Kwi-hyen, said Daewoo was still pursuing the sale and French workers should have no concerns over jobs or welfare.

The federation, which represents South Korea's mighty business conglomerates, known as "chaebol", later released an English copy of the letter to ambassador Dominique Perreau, and the language was slightly less harsh.
"Especially, there is concern among the Korean business community that there would appear to be no solid economic grounds for such a decision," it said.
"As a result, this action has aroused doubts concerning France's impartiality towards non-European investors and her commitment to globalisation."
French businessmen in South Korea were worried that the Thomson fiasco could sour the business relationship.

South Korea plans to spend billions of dollars to upgrade the infrastructure and modernise its armed forces over the next several years, and French companies are well placed to pick up contracts for nuclear power plants, railway equipment and possibly fighter jets.
The letter noted that French and Korean business cooperation was in a "golden age", and said the timing of the French decision was unfortunate.
